title: Beyond tables: images in the engine, their near copies and their scenes caught
request: Phase 4: extend DCLab beyond tables to image classification and other uses.
spec: The embedded machine reads images from pixel columns (pixel_prefix), encodes them with a centred local baseline, finds near copies on the pixels, holds out whole scenes; the shapes replica as an image table; the image acceptance; the code export.
plan: Keep images inside the embedded kind, as image tables come (pixels as columns).
Find copies on the pictures, classify on features.
Check the trap is caught on several seeds, not only that the split is by scene.
Image decision points with known truths: near copies across sources, suspect labels, whether a flip keeps the label.
Plant their traps in the shapes replica from a separate stream so its defaults stay byte-identical.
Generate per-point sets with a sealed partition by table, through the builder the tabular sets use.

decisions.decision: Images stay in the embedded kind, not a new kind.
decisions.why: The kind already owns the words for images; a second kind would split the Home's detection.

decisions.decision: Near copies are found on pixels averaged to a grid, not on the classifier's features.
decisions.why: Features built to classify pull every image of a class together: a copy and another image of its class looked alike.

decisions.decision: Images join self-play as a variant of the embedded kind, not a kind of their own.
decisions.why: The engine runs them as the embedded machine; the problem_type answer must name an engine kind, so the variant answers 'embedded' while its group keeps the image name.

decisions.decision: An image table's pixel columns are one column state in the examples.
decisions.why: 1,024 pixel states would drown the question and teach nothing a pixel's band says; the count and the side are what a decision needs.

decisions.decision: Three yes-or-no points on subject project, keyed by rows, not a new subject kind.
decisions.why: A new subject kind changes the ledger contract's schema; a key naming rows keeps the contract and the main product's reading.

decisions.decision: The near-copy question asks about pairs of different sources only.
decisions.why: Shots of one scene are already kept on one side by the split; the trap the scene column cannot see is a subject filed again under another name.

decisions.decision: The flip is measured, not assumed: a classifier fitted on half the sources, scored on the others as they are and mirrored.
decisions.why: Whether a flip keeps a label depends on what the label means (a circle, an arrow); only the images say it.

decisions.decision: The engine records at most 1,500 training images' decisions, 200 suspect and 200 other labels, and reports totals before the caps.
decisions.why: The comparison is quadratic and a person reads the evidence: a capped count shown as a total would understate the trap.

decisions.decision: The sets go to generated_images_v1 and models_images_v1, apart from the tabular ones.
decisions.why: The tabular models' sealed gate was run once (22.3); adding points to its folder would mix spent and unseen sets.

change: embeddings (Pixels, Centred, pixel_columns, images_of, calibrate sources), shapes_table, EmbeddedMachine image path, image_case and accept_image_engine, code export of images. Then images in self-play: a variant kind solved by the engine (selfplay.py _Images), pixels as one column state, forget() and --again. Then its decision points: dclab_core.image_decisions (rule_decisions, decide), three ledger points and their state fields, the replica's traps (reshot, mislabel, arrows), the image machine's leakage stage recording them, decisions_gen --images, decision_models_build --images, the lake reading the image sets. With two 26.5 harness and product fixes found in a live run.

findings.defect: An existing acceptance test counted the new image checks as text checks.
findings.scenario: The test filtered checks by their prefix and found 7, not 5.
findings.cause: The image checks shared the text checks' wording.
findings.fix: The image checks are named images: and asserted beside the texts.

findings.defect: The near-copy trap was not caught: the check passed by 0.0002 at one seed and failed at another.
findings.scenario: Every pair of images had a cosine near 0.998; two shots of a scene counted as different pairs in calibration.
findings.cause: Rectified pooled features are all alike, and calibration ignored the sources.
findings.fix: Copies are found on pixels; calibration leaves same-source pairs out; the check requires most shot pairs flagged and almost no other pair, on seeds 0 to 3.

findings.defect: Pixel columns were ordered as text.
findings.scenario: pixel10 came before pixel2: an MNIST-style table's images were scrambled.
findings.fix: Ordered by the number after the prefix; a name without one is refused.

findings.defect: An image project's code export would not run.
findings.scenario: It read a text column that images do not have.
findings.fix: The export writes the image path and reproduces the holdout.

findings.defect: A forbidden pixel was still read while the evidence said kept out.
findings.scenario: The person forbids px_0042 as a watermark.
findings.cause: The image branch skipped the text branch's checks.
findings.fix: A forbidden pixel and a source equal to the target are refused when the solution is saved.

findings.defect: The check demanded no near copy across the holdout line.
findings.scenario: At seed 3 two scenes that look alike sit on both sides: 16 pairs.
findings.cause: A scene's shots never straddle the line; two alike scenes may.
findings.fix: The engine reports and warns about them; the check asks that they are reported, not absent.

findings.defect: The embedded kind's split examples named no group column.
findings.scenario: An image solve's split_design answer gave group_column None although the holdout is whole scenes; the 36 earlier split examples of the notes (by author) had the same gap.
findings.cause: The embedded kind keeps its group as kind_fields.source_column, not group_column.
findings.fix: examples_of reads the source column as the group; selfplay --again --kinds embedded solves the earlier problems again whole.

findings.defect: The near-copy set held no negative pair.
findings.scenario: A table with 8 scenes filed again: their 128 pairs over the threshold filled the 120 questions.
findings.cause: Pairs over the threshold were taken first, up to the whole cap.
findings.fix: At most half the questions are over the threshold, spread over their similarities; the rest are the closest pairs below it.

findings.defect: An outcome recorded in words turned a column only mentioned into the outcome.
findings.scenario: 'Whether a subscriber cancels their plan at renewal' with a plan column: the outcome became plan and the question was closed.
findings.cause: The 26.5 fix matched any whole-word column name, around the 20.10 guard.
findings.fix: A column counts only in backticks, opening the words, or as 'the X column', and never in a clause that says it is known later.

findings.defect: A regression image table got label and flip decisions that meant nothing.
findings.scenario: 800 images with a number label: all 800 labels suspect, the flip safe at accuracy 0.
findings.fix: A number label is asked about near copies only.

findings.defect: The leakage evidence showed capped counts as totals.
findings.scenario: 5,000 near copies across sources read as 60.
findings.cause: The summary counted the kept records.
findings.fix: The rules count totals before any cap; the evidence names the recorded counts apart.

findings.defect: The written person confirmed the outcome column in answer to another question.
findings.scenario: 'Is the price known when the listing is posted?' answered as a confirmation of price.
findings.cause: The confirmation ran before the meaning patterns, with a loose pattern.
findings.fix: It runs last, only on a yes-or-no question that the column is the outcome.

findings.defect: Leave to build was given while the stop's own question was open.
findings.scenario: The card waited for the prediction moment; the agent's words also offered a build; the person said build.
findings.cause: The build request was read before the blocker.
findings.fix: The blocker is answered first; leave to build only when nothing else is asked.

findings.defect: The training-only test could not fail.
findings.scenario: It changed held-out images and passed only training ones to the rule.
findings.cause: It tested the function, not the engine.
findings.fix: The engine's machine is built, every key checked against its training rows, and changed held-out images and labels shown to move nothing.

measurements.name: the image decision sets (generated_images_v1)
measurements.gate: each point has a sealed partition by table, the rebuilt sets have the same sealed fingerprints, and both labels occur
measurements.result: 80 tables, 37,200 decisions: image.near_copy 9,600 (5,236 yes; rules right 0.849), image.label_suspect 27,520 (964 yes; rules right 0.992), image.flip_safe 80 (40 yes; rules right 1.0); sealed 2,160, 6,200 and 18
measurements.against_gate: Every set has a sealed partition and both labels; the test rebuilds them with the same fingerprints.
limits: Invented images with planted traps: a score on them says how a model reads these traps, not real photographs.
The flip set has 80 tables: one decision per table.

outcome: Images run in the engine to their holdout, their near copies and scenes caught on four seeds, and their code reproduces the number. Its decision points are recorded by the engine and generated with their truths, ready for decision models.
lessons: Find copies on the data itself; a classifier's features are built to make different items alike.
When a kind keeps a common fact under its own field, every consumer that reads the common field silently gets None: read both, and test the answer, not only that the solve verified.
A capped sample of records is not the count a person reads: count before the cap.
A fix that reads a column from words must keep every guard the reader already had.
risks: The encoder is a baseline, not pretrained; decision sets for image points are not built.
